Alabama Governor's Mansion

For more than sixty years, the Alabama Governor’s Mansion has stood as a testament to the state’s rich history, hospitality, and leadership. Since acquiring the current mansion in 1950, thirteen First Families have called it home, raising children, hosting dignitaries, and conducting official state business. It remains a beacon of tradition, blending historical preservation with modern governance.

A Storied Past

The first official residence for Alabama’s governor was acquired in 1911. Prior to that, governors resided in private homes or local hotels. The original mansion, a Beaux Arts brownstone, was located at the intersection of South Perry and South Streets in Montgomery. Purchased for $46,500, it was home to several governors until 1950, when it was repurposed as a state office building before its eventual demolition in 1963.

The current mansion, located at 1142 South Perry Street, was originally built in 1907 for Robert Fulwood Ligon, Jr. Designed in the Neoclassical Revival style by architect Weatherly Carter, the house was purchased by the state for $100,000, with an additional $130,000 spent on renovations. Governor Gordon Persons and his family were the first to reside there, moving in on his inauguration day, January 15, 1951.

Architectural Grandeur

The Alabama Governor’s Mansion is a stunning example of Classical Revival architecture. Its grand exterior features a Corinthian composite tetrastyle portico, intricate wrought iron balconies, and an ornate Ionic porte-cochère. Inside, the mansion boasts 17 primary rooms, with a magnificent double staircase at the entrance. The mansion grounds span two acres and include a formal garden, a guest house, a stone grotto, and a swimming pool shaped like the state of Alabama.

Preserving a Legacy

In 2011, the Alabama Legislature passed the Mansion Preservation Act, ensuring that the 117-year-old house remains historically accurate and well-maintained. The act established an authority responsible for overseeing its restoration and preservation efforts, ensuring that future generations can appreciate this historic landmark.

A Home for the People

Beyond being the residence of Alabama’s First Family, the mansion serves as a public treasure. Thanks to preservation efforts, it is open for tours, inviting visitors to experience Alabama’s history and hospitality firsthand. The First Lady and various organizations have worked tirelessly to maintain its grandeur and make it accessible to the public.

About the Mansion Tour

Free guided tours are available from January 16, 2024, through October 29, 2024, upon reservation, with a 60-person capacity, on the days and times listed below. Additionally, the Governor’s Mansion Gift Shop will be open during this timeframe.

Scheduled tours will resume on January 16, 2025. Please join us for the free Holiday Candlelight Tours in December. Information for these tours can be found below. Reservations must be made at least 48 hours in advance and are on a first-come, first-served basis. Walk-up tours are unavailable.

Tour Details:

  • Duration: 30-45 minutes
  • Days: Tuesdays and Thursdays
  • Times: 9 a.m., 10 a.m., 2 p.m., and 3 p.m.
  • Reservations: Submit the form below or contact us at Tours@mansion.alabama.gov or call 334-425-2818.
  • Requirements: Each group must bring a complete list of attendees (first and last name) to submit to security upon arrival.

Holiday Candlelight Tour Dates 2024

Holiday Candlelight Tours will occur on:

  • Monday, December 9: 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.
  • Monday, December 16: 2:00 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. or 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

This is a FREE self-guided tour that requires a ticket to enter. Beginning October 28, 2024, tickets will be available at:

  • Governor’s Mansion Gift Shop (30 Finley Avenue, Montgomery, AL 36104)
  • Sweet Home Alabama Gift Shop (401 Adams Avenue, Montgomery, AL 36104)

For questions regarding the Holiday Candlelight Tours, please contact us at tours@mansion.alabama.gov or call 334-425-2818.

Request a Mansion Tour We encourage all Alabamians and visitors to explore this remarkable piece of history. Whether through a guided tour or a special event, the Alabama Governor’s Mansion remains a proud symbol of our state’s past, present, and future.
